crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Generating assessments covers the use of AI systems to produce quiz questions, exam items, rubrics, and practice problems for courses. It sits within course design and teaching, where the output is a draft that an instructor reviews rather than a finished instrument. The work spans multiple choice, short answer, essay prompts, and scenario based tasks, and it draws on the course's own learning objectives and source materials.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Most tools in this space are built on large language models accessed through a chat interface or an API, with retrieval over the instructor's own notes, textbook chapters, or slide decks. Some platforms add a question bank, a learning management system integration, and item statistics from prior cohorts.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The common workflow starts with a learning objective and a passage of source text, then prompts the model to write items at a stated difficulty and cognitive level. Instructors check each item for factual accuracy, alignment with the objective, and plausible but clearly wrong distractors. Many teams generate more items than they need, discard the weak ones, and keep a reviewed set in a bank for reuse. Where the source is a research paper, linking to the original paper rather than a summary keeps the provenance traceable.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risks are hallucinated facts, items that leak answer keys, and questions that reproduce copyrighted text or student work without permission. Institutions increasingly require a human reviewer of record, a note on which model and prompt produced each item, and a check that the item has not appeared in a public question bank. Assessment content also touches student data protection when past responses are used as examples, and accessibility standards apply to the final format. None of this is legal advice, and policies vary by institution and jurisdiction.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect tighter integration between item generation and learning analytics, so that a generated question can be traced to the objective it tests and to the cohort data that shows whether it works. Adaptive and personalized practice sets are likely to become more common, along with stronger provenance metadata on every item. The open questions are how much review is enough and how to keep a bank from drifting out of date as the underlying subject changes.
